speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: asked	the Minister for Manpower in light of the increase in numbers of workers participating in the "sharing" economy with many being freelancers or self-employed (a) whether has there been a deflationary impact on wages in sectors with a high concentration of such workers; and (b) how can the Government help these workers to be financially adequate in their retirement.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: This will help us better understand the profiles of freelancers, including whether they take up freelancing as a primary or secondary source of income, as well as the sectors and occupations they are in.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: With the information from the survey, we will monitor more closely the workforce trends of the "sharing economy" and look into the issues that freelancers may face, including retirement adequacy.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: I would just like to have two points of clarification.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The first one, especially in the areas he had pointed out, in terms of Uber and Grab driving affecting the taxi companies, whether the income of the taxi drivers has been affected?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: And secondly, can the Ministry consider Codes of Best Practices for Government contractors to take on certain practices that help freelancers prepare for their retirement, including contributions to CPF?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: One sector saw a drop of about 1% a year, and that was in real estate services.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Another sector which saw a fairly stagnant median income is finance and insurance services.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For all the other sectors, including transportation and storage, there was a broad-based real wage increase over the three years.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: But having said that, I think past performance may not necessarily be an indication of future performance.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: What we are concerned about is whether, in time to come, the growth of this so-called gig economy will have a greater impact on more workers.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: And that is the reason why we have decided to initiate this new series of annual surveys.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I would only be able to better answer the question raised by the Member after the tripartite partners have had the chance to look at these survey findings for last year and, subsequently, on a year-to-year basis for us to analyse further in terms of what are the best practices, as the Member has proposed, as well as what we can do together to strengthen the retirement adequacy of these workers.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Will the Ministry look into increasing communication and education for these freelancing workers so that they are aware of the risk that is involved in terms of overall financial planning for them when they are engaged in freelancing jobs?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We will always be concerned for them in terms of their savings for housing and retirement.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, as I have said earlier, the tripartite partners intend to focus on this and see how we can reach out to more of them and, hopefully, put in place various measures ‒ maybe on the part of the freelancers themselves or their customers' service buyers ‒ to see how we can work together to strengthen their retirement adequacy.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I just want to check whether the survey will also cover liabilities, because the gig economy is very different from that for traditional freelancers in which there are lots of established norms.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: If we look at Uber and others, for example, they do have other liabilities which they cater for as well and they are also at risk, but also in terms of income.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I am glad the Minister has also mentioned and talked about the concerns about OA and SA contributions.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Has there been a study today on the impact of the gig economy on the ability to service housing loans and insurance coverage and all that?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For the freelancers, we may ask them through informal surveys, "How do you prepare for your housing and retirement?" They will say, "Look, since I do not contribute to OA and SA, I have saved for it myself." If you ask the taxi driver, "Do you save enough to pay for your housing?" He will say, "Yes, I have." "Are you saving enough for your retirement?" He will say, "Yes, I am." This is based on the present situation.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In a way, our concern about housing, medical and retirement needs of freelancers is not a new issue.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: It has been around for the last many years because freelancers have been around in the market for a long, long time.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We are not jumping to any conclusion at this moment because, firstly, we would like to know whether more and more of them are primary freelancers or secondary freelancers.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In other words, with the growth of the sharing economy, workers who have their primary employment are now taking advantage of sharing platforms to earn additional income, which may not be a bad thing.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: But as I have said, I do not want to prejudge the outcome of our analysis at this moment.
